source.objectiveEnglish: greet staff, learn whether to order at the counter, and find a place
source.roleplayEnglish: Walk into a crowded Roman café and work out how ordering and seating operate.

sourceVerbExamples.target: Un viajero entra en un café muy lleno.
sourceVerbExamples.native: A traveler enters a very busy café.

sourceVerbExamples.target: Después pide un café y pan dulce.
sourceVerbExamples.native: Then he orders a coffee and a sweet pastry.
He asks: Is there a free table?

archivedDraft.scene: Sam enters a busy café near a station and asks the staff how to order.

sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: In some places people also say cola.
Common in Mexican and US Spanish.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Buenos días, ¿pido aquí en el mostrador?
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Good morning, do I order here at the counter?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: おはようございます。こちらのカウンターで注文すればいいですか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Good morning. Should I order at this counter?

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 空いているテーブルはありますか。

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Do I sit wherever I want?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 好きなところに座ってもいいですか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: May I sit wherever I like?

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Perdón, no entiendo. ¿Puede repetir, por favor?
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Sorry, I don't understand. Can you repeat, please?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: すみません、わかりません。もう一度言っていただけますか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Excuse me, I do not understand. Could you say it again?

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: ¿Es para llevar o para comer aquí?
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Is it to go or to eat here?
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Staff often ask this; you can also say it to check.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: お持ち帰りですか、それとも店内でお召し上がりですか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Will you take it away or eat in? (staff-side polite wording)
sourceCards.speakerUse: staff-to-customer; traveler-side version requires separate review

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Un viajero entra en un café muy lleno.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: A traveler enters a very busy café.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者が、とても混んでいるカフェに入ります。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: A traveler enters a very crowded café.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Hay una fila larga frente al mostrador.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: There is a long line in front of the counter.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カウンターの前には長い列があります。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: There is a long line in front of the counter.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者は言います。「おはようございます。」

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Pregunta a la mesera: ¿Pido aquí en el mostrador?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: He asks the waitress: Do I order here at the counter?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者は女性の店員に聞きます。「こちらのカウンターで注文すればいいですか。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The traveler asks a female staff member: Should I order at this counter?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La mesera contesta: Sí, pida aquí, por favor.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The waitress answers: Yes, order here, please.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 女性の店員は答えます。「はい、こちらでご注文ください。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The female staff member answers: Yes, please order here.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: He asks: Is there a free table?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者は聞きます。「空いているテーブルはありますか。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The traveler asks: Is there an available table?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La mesera dice: Hay una mesa en la terraza.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The waitress says: There is a table on the patio.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 女性の店員は言います。「テラスにテーブルがあります。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The female staff member says: There is a table on the terrace.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Él espera en la fila y mira el menú.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: He waits in line and looks at the menu.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 旅行者は列に並んで待ち、メニューを見ます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The traveler waits in line and looks at the menu.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Después pide un café y pan dulce.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Then he orders a coffee and a sweet pastry.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: それから、コーヒーとパン・ドゥルセを注文します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Then the traveler orders coffee and pan dulce.

speakingGoalCandidate: Greet the waitress, ask whether to order at the counter, and ask whether a table is available in a busy café.
japaneseSpecificFocusCandidate: Ask service-process and seating questions with ～すればいいですか, ～はありますか and ～てもいいですか; source Spanish verb classes are not a Japanese conjugation lesson.

unresolvedInternal: Source plan says Roman café; the Spanish Reader names no city and uses Mexican pan dulce. Choose intended locale before learner promotion.
Spanish café means the shop and may also mean coffee; Japanese カフェ carries only the shop sense here.
Spanish mesero/mesera has grammatical gender; Japanese 店員 is neutral. Reader retains a female staff member.
Pan dulce is preserved as a source-specific term, not silently generalized to Japanese sweet bread; qualified food/locale wording needed.
Card 15 is a staff-side question, so its Japanese polite register differs from traveler-side prompts.
Japanese quote punctuation, terrace seating, table availability and service register need qualified review.
The pinned Spanish Reader itself is reviewed:false; source text is not qualified approval.
Pin 空いている as あいている (vacant), not すいている (uncrowded), before any audio synthesis.
